vo: Welcome. In the next few minutes, I'll walk you through setting up your very first Bot employee, step by step.
You don't need to code. Start from zero, watch this once, and follow along.
AI agents have evolved. First came the chat box. Then came coding agents, powerful, but hard to start. Now there's a personal agent that works inside your own business.
And it really isn't hype. It's an all-day team of Bots, and the real work goes to them.
Step one: install. Just download it from the official site, open it, and sign in.
It's not another chat box, and it's not a coding agent either. Think of it as a truly smart assistant.
Create your first Bot in four steps. New, pick an avatar, give it a name, and set its rules. I named mine Translator.
There's a big directory of ready-made Bots for marketing, design, hiring, and operations. You can also connect your tools, like Notion, your calendar, or your mail.
Before this, none of my devices talked to each other. Every phone and computer was its own little world.
Now they're all linked, and there are no walls between them.
The same Bot works everywhere. Log in on your phone, and one sentence is all it takes.
Now, real business.
My company has three real business departments, and every department is a team of Bots.
Every Bot gets one job. A job description is simply a skill. For example, a topic picker that sends me the best ideas every morning.
Another Bot finds footage for my edits, and puts it into an editing project.
Jobs hand work to each other. Pick a topic, write, design, then edit. Each role is a mature skill, like an employee handbook. Use it first, add rules, add limits, and it gets sharper every time.
The design Bot makes the covers directly, in every size I need.
That design skill is open source, and I wrote beginner docs to go with it.
For important departments, you can assign a manager Bot. You can't direct every employee yourself, so scheduling is the key.
On my Windows computer, a fixed script handles the editing.
Every day at five thirty, it cuts the video from my desktop assets, publishes it, and fills the links back in.
Put it together and you have a one-person company. A chief Bot, an editor, a copywriter, a publisher, and an asset manager, each reporting back when the job is done.
Some people say its code isn't top-tier, or its images aren't the best. But think like a boss. You don't need the best at everything. You need to orchestrate.
A few quick-launch tips.
There are two quick ways to call it. Bind it to your side button, or just say, Hey Bot.
For the side button, check two things: the latest app version, and an iPhone with an Action button.
Open Shortcuts, create Start Voice Chat, and select the Bot you just made.
Prefer taps? Go to Accessibility, then Touch, then Back Tap, and pick a double or triple tap.
For voice, say Hey Bot three times to record it. It can even handle your calendar, reminders, and alarms.
Now, a few pitfalls.
First, it tends to over-correct. A small edit turns into a rewrite. My fix: hand code changes to a coding tool, or use a script I've already tuned.
Second, there's no separate window for each Bot yet. I've sent the feedback, and I hope it arrives soon.
And the biggest trap of all: spending more time designing the org chart than doing real work.
Be rational, and do the math first. You invest a subscription and some setup time. You should get back saved time and real results. Otherwise, it's meaningless.
I use coding tools constantly, and the usage adds up fast. But they always felt bloated.
Now it's minimal. Simple interaction, a digital company structure, and everything driven by your real business.
Think about drinking water. Swap a heavy jug for a case of bottled water, and it gets easier.
Habits work the same way. Shorten the chain. Have an idea, call your Bot from anywhere, and hand it off. The smoother it feels, the more you use it.
Even on a business trip, or on a beach, it's one tap away.
My dream is a scene like this: commanding a whole team, planning from far away, like a strategist.
So start small. One Bot, one real task. Build everything around your real business, and let it work for you.
